page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m2.large is a shared-core virtual machine instance belonging to the economy ecs.e family. Powered by the KVM hypervisor on an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, the instance provisions 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with multithreading enabled. The CPU provides a 33 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and vector instruction extensions including AVX and AVX-512F alongside cryptographic AES support. System memory totals 4.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes no bundled local storage, operating purely on network-attached storage, and provides no GPU acceleration capabilities.

Benchmark measurements indicate entry-level execution limits characteristic of shared compute infrastructure. Multi-core compute performance sits within the bottom 10 percent of recorded benchmarks, reflected in a PassMark CPU score of 1747.41 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 808.0. Single-core stress-ng tests reached 1301.89, while uncached memory read and write bandwidth both registered near 2.0 GB/s. Application tests show similarly modest throughput, achieving 0.28 GB/s in static web serving, 536.8 operations in PassMark database testing, and 1.39 million operations per second in Redis SET operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU allocation minimizes resource commitments for lightweight tasks where hardware utilization is sporadic. The instance presents noticeable tradeoffs, specifically shared vCPU resource contention and constrained memory throughput that restrict high-throughput I/O or parallel compilation. Consequently, the ecs.e-c1m2.large is appropriate for non-critical development and test setups, basic internal tools, low-traffic web hosting, and background administrative jobs rather than production-grade data processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m2.large is an entry-tier virtual server from the shared ecs.e family designed for low-demand operational environments. Built on an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz, the instance delivers 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core with multithreading, accompanied by 4.0 GB of system memory. It does not provide onboard local storage or dedicated GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage architectures. Performance testing reflects its shared-core configuration, placing multi-threaded processing, Geekbench scores, and uncached memory bandwidth in the lower tiers of comparative benchmarks. Database handling reaches 536.8 PassMark database operations, and Redis records 1.39 million SET operations per second. While unsuited for resource-heavy workloads, its low resource overhead offers qualitative economy for non-critical developer testbeds, light administrative agents, and modest web-serving tasks.
